conventions.convention: Natural units ħ=c=1; Minkowski signature (-+++); spatial orientation ε123=1; smooth static fields on all of R³, with A0=0 and identically zero Higgs potential.
The global group is SU(2), with fundamental-doublet external probes, Ta=-iσa/2, [Ta,Tb]=εabcTc, and κ(X,Y)=-2Tr₂(XY), so κ(Ta,Tb)=δab.

Right principal-bundle section changes use Aj=Ad(hij⁻¹)Ai+hij⁻¹dhij and Φj=Ad(hij⁻¹)Φi. Curvature, covariant derivative, and magnetic field are Fij=∂iAj-∂jAi+[Ai,Aj], DiΦ=∂iΦ+[Ai,Φ], and Bi=εijkFjk/2.

The asymptotic reduction is an adopted boundary hypothesis: Φ(R·)/v converges in C∞; adapted angular connections converge pointwise to C1 extensions; their curvatures converge uniformly to the curvature of those extensions; the limiting tangential derivative vanishes. B∞ is the scaled radial limit R²ωiBi(Rω), not the unscaled magnetic field.
The equator is oriented as ∂DN, uS=uNh, h=exp(θT3), and ν=-(θ(2π)-θ(0))/(4π). Consequently positive ν corresponds to positive magnetic surface charge.

E=(2g²)⁻¹∫Σi(κ(Bi,Bi)+κ(DiΦ,DiΦ)); m is the outward surface integral of κ(Φ,Bi); T=m/g². Here g>0 is dimensionless and v>0 has dimension length⁻¹. BPS denotes classical energy saturation without identifying a quantum state or supersymmetry central charge.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the smooth static SU(2) adjoint-Higgs zero-potential model on R³, its energy E=(2g²)⁻¹∫Σi(κ(Bi,Bi)+κ(DiΦ,DiΦ)), the specified asymptotic reduction and fundamental-doublet probe data, and the magnetic surface charge m with T=g⁻²m. The boundary convergence and reduction conditions are adopted hypotheses, not asserted consequences of finite energy.

For smooth finite-energy fields under the stated static-sector and surface-limit hypotheses, E=(2g²)⁻¹∫Σiκ(Bi-DiΦ,Bi-DiΦ)+T and E=(2g²)⁻¹∫Σiκ(Bi+DiΦ,Bi+DiΦ)-T. Hence E≥|T|. Equality is equivalent to Bi=DiΦ everywhere for T>0, Bi=-DiΦ everywhere for T<0, and Bi=DiΦ=0 everywhere for T=0.
Under the stated SU(2) asymptotic reduction, transition-lift, orientation, convergence and surface-limit hypotheses, ν=-(θ(2π)-θ(0))/(4π) belongs to Z, m=4πvν, and T=4πvν/g².

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit inherited ACω assumption: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a selecting function. No stronger choice principle is introduced by the owned calculations.
Smoothness and the representation law for the adjoint action used to interpret the real Higgs field inside the complexified adjoint representation.

Flux proof step 3.1 applies C1 Stokes separately to the closed hemispheres with their opposite induced equatorial orientations. These hemispheres satisfy the supplier's boundary regularity hypotheses.
Energy proof step 2.1 applies divergence to the smooth real vector field Ji=κ(Φ,Bi) on each bounded ball before taking the infinite-radius limit.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier's BPS-state definition and N=2 saturation theorem against the classical consumers. This is a contextual page prerequisite: the owned items explicitly exclude quantum-state, representation and central-charge identifications, and do not use the Hilbert-space result as a premise.

The actual item supplier is the SU(2) invariant-form lemma. Its anti-Hermitian basis, commutators, compactness and κ normalization agree with the sector and both proofs. The adjoint-Higgs energy is adopted separately.

Checked gauge data, principal connection, graded bracket, associated derivative and Cartan–Bianchi suppliers. Their right-action signs, half-bracket curvature normalization and local Bianchi identity agree with the owned definitions and proof uses.

The example uses the invariant-form lemma's exact εabc bracket and κ(Ta,Tb)=δab normalization. Its negative radial Higgs profile and positive curvature convention consistently give Bi=DiΦ, m=4πv and ν=1.
